title: Carbon Hub — Overview
summary: A plain-English guide to what Carbon is building, where the work stands, and what each development step changes.
audience_rule: Assume the reader knows nothing about Carbon, Bittensor, scientific machine learning, or the repository. Explain the idea first; expose canonical Carbon terms in Technical Detail.

A.title: Build the trustworthy software foundation
A.what: Build the basic software boundaries Carbon needs before it can run a real scientific competition: define safe submissions, protect hidden tests, score by fixed rules, separate private evidence from public results, and track failures cleanly.
A.why: Later science is only credible if the software keeps competitors, evaluators, protected test information, public outputs, and economic state from silently taking control of one another.
A.done_when: Carbon can demonstrate the intended boundaries with controlled test fixtures and automated checks.
A.not_yet: This does not mean Carbon has a scientifically qualified exam, a live Bittensor market, production security, or real emissions.

B.title: Define the exam and research loop
B.what: Define exactly how one physics problem is described, how test cases are created, what counts as a reference answer, how a candidate is measured, and how researchers can practice against the system.
B.why: Carbon cannot fairly test or compare models until the problem, reference answers, measurements, resource limits, and research interface mean one exact thing.
B.done_when: Carbon can run the complete research and exam workflow with controlled test fixtures while the system still refuses to call those fixtures real scientific qualification.
B.not_yet: This does not yet mean Carbon can run a live scientific Challenge, publish Bittensor weights from real scientific results, or claim scientific qualification.

C.title: Connect Carbon to Bittensor and run one real test path
C.what: Connect participant identity and authenticated requests to Bittensor, then run one real candidate through Carbon's protected evaluation path and prove temporary testnet weight publication.
C.why: Carbon needs to prove that Bittensor can carry identity and incentives without letting chain mechanics decide scientific truth.
C.done_when: A real candidate can move from an authenticated Bittensor identity through protected evaluation to a temporary testnet result that can be read back and expired safely.
C.not_yet: Testnet publication does not make the science live, qualify the Challenge, create a frontier advance, settle rewards, or authorize mainnet.

D.title: Prove the first exam is scientifically fit for purpose
D.what: Have the responsible scientific owners decide and document the real physics envelope, test population, reference hierarchy, measurements, uncertainty rules, thresholds, security evidence, and activation conditions.
D.why: Passing software tests cannot prove that an exam measures the physical claim Carbon says it measures.
D.done_when: The first exact Challenge has enough reviewed scientific and security evidence to be activated for its registered purpose.
D.not_yet: One qualified Challenge does not prove product qualification, commercial repeatability, frontier advancement, or reward settlement.

E.title: Learn from past experiments without changing the judge
E.what: Store structured experiment results and use them to suggest better research directions, future experiments, and useful history.
E.why: Carbon should get smarter as experiments accumulate, but learned patterns must not rewrite a live exam after results are known.
E.done_when: Past evidence can produce traceable research suggestions while registered exam rules remain the authority.
E.not_yet: Learned history cannot define truth, alter a current exam, expose hidden tests, or revise an existing result.

F.title: Decide whether one exact model is fit for one real job
F.what: Take a specific model and test the exact artifact, runtime, deployment context, limitations, and conditions under which it can support a defined engineering use.
F.why: Winning a research competition is weaker evidence than showing that a specific deployed model can support a specific customer decision.
F.done_when: Carbon can state what one exact model can support, where it cannot be relied on, and what changes would force re-testing.
F.not_yet: A high Challenge score does not qualify a product, and evidence for one component does not qualify an entire system.

G.title: Connect customer work to Carbon without weakening the science
G.what: Define how enterprise programs handle privacy, rights, reference access, deliverables, payment, acceptance, and lifecycle while keeping scientific rules independent.
G.why: Customers need private and contractable workflows, but commercial pressure cannot change what the evidence means.
G.done_when: Carbon can structure enterprise programs with explicit rights, privacy, truth access, deliverables, payment, and lifecycle controls.
G.not_yet: A designed commercial product or privacy mode is not a live capability until the required technical and commercial qualification exists.

H.title: Prove when the scientific frontier really moved
H.what: Separate an ordinary leaderboard result from stronger evidence that a new contender beat the accepted frontier on comparable fresh tests.
H.why: A slightly higher score or temporary first place is not enough to prove a genuine scientific advance.
H.done_when: Carbon can record a frontier advance only when the registered comparison resolves it, including the option to say the evidence is inconclusive.
H.not_yet: Being the incumbent does not create permanent reward rights, and unresolved evidence does not create a winner.

I.title: Turn verified scientific events into network settlement
I.what: Build the treasury, accounting, validator-service, and payment path that converts finalized scientific events into exact network obligations without changing the underlying scientific result.
I.why: Mainnet economics need auditable accounting, safe retries, custody, and proof that validators perform useful work.
I.done_when: Carbon can trace a finalized scientific event through an exact obligation and settlement path, including rollback and migration evidence.
I.not_yet: Treasury or chain behavior cannot create, erase, or change scientific merit, and mainnet still requires separate activation approval.

J.title: Let different kinds of fast physics models compete fairly
J.what: Add qualified ways to rebuild and evaluate more model families, such as neural operators, reduced-order models, and hybrid systems.
J.why: Carbon should judge whether a method solves the physical job, not favor one architecture label.
J.done_when: Different model families can enter through registered interfaces and face the same applicable scientific requirements.
J.not_yet: No model family receives scientific preference because it is neural, mechanistic, symbolic, hybrid, or popular.

K.title: Let researchers search for whole model-building methods
K.what: Expand the competition from tuning a bounded training recipe toward proposing richer ways to construct a fast physical model.
K.why: The best improvement may come from architecture, objectives, representations, solver hybrids, or staged procedures rather than parameter tuning.
K.done_when: Researchers and agents can propose broader construction methods while Carbon's independent evaluator still controls the official measurements and grade.
K.not_yet: A construction method cannot inspect the official evaluator or define the measurements that prove its own success.

L.title: Run broader model-building methods in isolation
L.what: Create a controlled reconstruction environment that can execute richer construction methods, record what happened, and hand the resulting model to the independent evaluator.
L.why: Broader model-building freedom creates security, reproducibility, dependency, and resource risks that must be controlled before official evaluation.
L.done_when: A registered construction method can produce an exact artifact and receipt inside an isolated environment, then cross a hard boundary into evaluation.
L.not_yet: Arbitrary participant code is not a default capability; broader execution requires separate security and scientific qualification.

M.title: Keep model evidence valid as real systems change
M.what: Track deployed models and systems through changes in models, data, solvers, hardware, operating envelopes, fallbacks, and deployment context.
M.why: Evidence for one exact system version can become stale when any important part of the system changes.
M.done_when: Carbon can preserve a model's evidence history and trigger requalification when a material change breaks the previous identity or claim.
M.not_yet: Success of an end-to-end system does not automatically validate every internal component or future version.

N.title: Prove Carbon's accumulated evidence helps make better future decisions
N.what: Test whether Carbon's evidence can improve choices such as which method to try, which experiment to run, where a model may fail, or which qualification evidence to collect next.
N.why: A convincing historical pattern is not enough; Carbon must show that the information improves the next registered decision.
N.done_when: Prospective tests show measurable decision improvement against a defined baseline, with known limits.
N.not_yet: Retrospective correlations or a polished dashboard do not establish useful Physics Intelligence.
